### Findings refused

- `l` of XXXIX 89 omits -ma of šayyāmānumma: kept. The -ma is a clause-initial marker (apodosis after the condition), not "and"; the note says so; an `and` in `l` would make the buyer's declaration read as part of the protasis.
- im-ta-ku-ut with `tr` "ku" (convention says KU read qu = qu₂): kept, because the latest published precedent (215-240, im-ku-ut-ma) writes `ku`; only `say` was corrected. Recorded as a possible house question for QUESTIONS.md.
- Lemma `pâqum` (ipaq, XXXIX 96): the circumflex implies a hollow verb the draft cannot show; Harper's lemma is PAKU "to receive into one's care, to be entrusted with" (confirmed in his glossary, 39, 96). No better lemma available from the sources; kept, UNCERTAIN, left to the glosser to phrase from Harper's entry.
- `bennī` (XXXIX 61): the -i is unexplained, honestly flagged in the note; Harper's glossary has bi-en-ni, "a kind of fever", exactly as the note says. Kept.
- `warḫušu` for Harper's arḫišu (XXXIX 60): kept; the glyphs are ITI + šu, the note says Harper's form and why.
- imlāma / `imlâ` (XXXIX 60): the preterite of malûm cannot be confirmed from the sources at hand; left, not flagged by the drafter either. A pass-2 point if the glosser can check the malûm entry.
- XXXIX 66 note ("a few more wedges than I can match"): kept as an honest uncertainty; Harper's reading i-li-qi₂ is the only one available and the sense is secure.
- "natives of the country" (XXXIX 83, 88): a common phrase, not distinctive of Harper; kept.
- "the silver he paid" (cf. Harper "the money which he paid"): derived from the published gloss of šaqālum ("to weigh out = to pay") and unit 64's `l`; kept.

### Plate checks

Plates 70 (lines 58–67) and 71 (lines 68–102) were viewed at zoom 3–9. Every line was checked at the level of sign groups against Harper's syllables; no sign misidentification found; I could not decide every wedge (rows 78–86 and 92–101 are dense). Confirmed on the plate: ARAD (one sign) and GEME₂ (SAL + KUR, two signs) stand bare, no -am/-im, in lines 59, 68, 75, 80, 83, 93 (and ARAD-zu / GEME₂-zu at 81, 96, 100); KÙ.BABBAR bare at 65, 91, 94, no -am; lines 62/63 break na-di-na- | -ni-šu; 69, 75, 88, 102 have half-rows (the second half carries no nl); u-te-id-di at 82 has four signs; line 85 has KÙ.BABBAR + ma; Column XL starts below line 102 on Plate 71. All 11 linecheck.md lines are logogram lines (ARAD, GEME₂, KÙ.BABBAR, DUMU{meš}, the ba-lum kaspi-ma line) and are confirmed as such.

### Disclosure check (§278–280 against Harper's own translation, p.115)

Looked at Harper's English of §278–280 only for this check. Verbatim overlap found: "male or female slave" (fixed, #19), "bennu" (a transliterated word, unavoidable), "natives of" / "without … money|silver" (common words, kept above). No other phrase is shared; the draft's wording differs in structure and verbs ("has bought" vs Harper's "sell"; "give him back to his seller" vs "return him to the seller"; "claims have arisen" vs "there be a claim upon him"; "has identified (?)" vs "recognize"; "hostile country" vs "foreign country"; "their release shall be set" vs "grant them their freedom").
Independence of the Akkadian readings: every form the draft analyses is in Harper's glossary under the entries the notes cite (BENNU "a kind of fever" 39, 61; BAKARU / BAKRU 39, 69, 71; MAKATU I,2 im-ta-ku-ut 39, 62; RASU I,2 ir-ta-si 39, 69; APALU i-ip-pa-al 39, 71; NUKURTU 39, 74; LIBBU li-ib-bu 39, 78; EDU II,2 u-te-id-di 39, 82; PAKU i-pa-ak 39, 96) and the drafter's grammar follows from them and from the published parts. The one place the draft disagrees with Harper's English is the right one (išāmma is "buys", a published gloss of šâmum-buy, not "sells"). Verdict: the readings are independently supported by the grammar and glossary; nothing looks borrowed from the translation.

`bennī … elīšu imtaqut` "the bennu-sickness has fallen on him" (bennu unread, "a sickness"); `ana nādinānišu utārma` "he shall give him back to his seller"; `baqrī irtaši` "claims have arisen against him (?)" (idiom, UNCERTAIN); `nādinānšu baqrī ippal` "his seller shall answer the claims"; `ina māt nukurtim` "in a hostile country"; `mārū mātim` "natives of the country" (`l` "sons-of the-land"); `utēddi` "has identified (?)" (D perfect of edûm, as uwaddīma §193); `ina maḫar ilim kaspam išqulu igabbima` "shall declare, before the god, the silver he paid"; `lū warassu lū amassu ipaq` "he shall take back (?) his male slave or his female slave" (ipaq UNCERTAIN, Harper PAKU); `ul bēlī atta` "You are not my master"; `kīma warassu ukānšuma` "he shall prove him to be his slave"; `uznašu inakkis` "he shall cut off his ear"; baqrī written with AK = aq; `i` phrase "a male or a female slave" (as §118). Changed from the draft: `imtaqut` (not imtakut); ba-aq-ri (not ba-ag-ri).

### Re-checks (pass-1 open points), no change

- imlāma: Harper's glossary lists MALU I,1 "to fill out, to complete: im-la, 39, 60"; the plate-form la-ma (long ā before -ma) fits a preterite imlâ + ma, so `say` imlāma and the lemma stand. The broaden entry now cites Harper.
- im-ta-ku-ut `tr` "ku": kept as in the published im-ku-ut-ma (215-240, sign KU, `tr` ku, Harper prints ku not ḳu); the note says the KU sign stands for qu. Inconsistent with the convention "KU read qu = qu₂" and with iš-qu₂-lu in the same part; QUESTIONS item (one house decision for both words).
- Lemma `pâqum`: kept (Harper PAKU; no better lemma; entry says UNCERTAIN and cites Harper).
- Units' `i`/`l`/notes re-read once more: l ↔ i force and wording consistent after pass 1; "and" placement across units 6/7 and 1 correct; no remembered English found.

### Findings refused

- Changing `tr` ku → qu₂ in im-ta-ku-ut: refused for this pass (latest published precedent; would split from im-ku-ut-ma; see QUESTIONS item).
- Dropping the dangling generic tags ("· verb", "· noun") inside old entries when appending: refused; "old entry whole" is the rule.
- "his month is not yet full" (unit 1 `i`) against `l` "has-been-full": a negative perfect reads as "is not yet full" in English; kept.
- Adding a separate lemma for the nominative/oblique mārū/mārê split: Harper's mârê is one reading of DUMU{meš}; kept as in the units.
